description: We are The Forgotten Rovers, bringing NASA’s rovers and equipment on the Moon and Mars to life through storytelling. Blending real mission facts with imagination, we’ll help children discover their adventures, scientific discoveries, and lasting legacy. We welcome teammates who enjoy story telling, writing, art, animation, and space exploration. Together, we’ll keep these explorers’ stories alive.
summary:
We Stayed Behind is a seven-slide storytelling presentation developed by The Forgotten Rovers. It follows the Apollo 17 lunar rover, Spirit, Opportunity, and Ingenuity through imagined first-person voices grounded in official NASA mission records and photographs.

Our project addresses the challenge by giving equipment left on the Moon and Mars a voice. Each explorer shares its purpose, challenges, discoveries, and the ending of its journey. We combined research with creative narration to make these true adventures accessible to young audiences.

These machines helped humans investigate the Moon’s volcanic past, discover evidence of ancient water on Mars, and demonstrate flight on another planet. Their stories show how teamwork and creative problem-solving make exploration possible. By sharing their achievements, we hope to inspire curiosity about space and encourage children to ask questions that future explorers could answer.
details:
We Stayed Behind, developed by The Forgotten Rovers, is a storytelling project presented through our combined 63-slide presentation. A separate seven-slide demo introduces the project and summarises its main ideas. Our 30-second speech explains how we approached the challenge as a team.

The full project explores the Apollo 17 lunar rover, Spirit, Opportunity, and Ingenuity. Each team member contributed research and storytelling material, which we combined into one presentation. Through imagined first-person voices, the explorers describe their purposes, challenges, discoveries, and final adventures. Official NASA mission records and photographs provide the factual foundation.

Our project addresses the challenge by sharing the histories of equipment left on the Moon and Mars. It highlights achievements such as the lunar rover’s improvised repair, the Mars rovers’ evidence of ancient water, and Ingenuity’s demonstration of powered flight on another planet.

The creative element is telling these adventures from the equipment’s perspective. Giving each explorer a voice helps audiences connect emotionally with its journey while learning about science and engineering. We aim to make space exploration accessible to young audiences and encourage curiosity, teamwork, and creative problem-solving.

Our tools included PowerPoint and PDF presentations, official NASA websites and image collections, and ChatGPT/Codex for AI-assisted research organisation, narration, editing, and presentation formatting. The finished project can be presented using a computer and projector.

We considered factual accuracy, clear identification of imagined storytelling, readable text, age-appropriate language, and contributions from every team member. For the separate demo, we selected the strongest examples and condensed them into seven slides, including the title and introduction.
